clue.text: This could make you afraid to go on

definitions.text: This could make you afraid to go on

parts.words: This could make you afraid to go on
parts.note: to go on means to walk out onto the boards before an audience, so the fear is the nerves an actor feels

explanation.surface: Something that makes a person too scared to carry on with life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go on' reads as 'continue', but in the theatre it means making an entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervousness before a performance can stop a performer from walking out in front of the audience.

definitions.meaning: to prune is to cut back
spruce as an adjective means neat and smart

explanation.definitionFit: To cut back a hedge is a synonym of the verb in the first; neat and smart is a synonym of spruce as an adjective.

definitions.meaning: lame, as in an injured, gammy leg

explanation.walkthrough: A 'game leg' is an old British phrase for a lame or injured leg; the question mark flags the less familiar sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up for anything is one sense; a lame leg is called a game leg in old British usage.

indicators.note: the word for well holds the fish inside it

parts.note: fit means well, in good health
the orfe is a freshwater fish, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: Admitting defeat while the well turns out to have fish in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something up as a penalty or loss is to surrender it.

indicators.note: for here means the word time is exchanged for a rearrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A moment set aside for doing a single task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a loose anagram signal: the letters of TIME are traded for another arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An individual article or unit on a list is a single thing.

clue.text: Got together for a discussion, perhaps, comedian Roy showed the way

definitions.text: Got together for a discussion, perhaps

parts.note: Roy Hudd was a British comedian and radio and television entertainer
to show the way is to lead, past tense led

explanation.surface: A comedian named Roy leading a group into a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Roy Hudd was a long-serving British comedian, known for radio shows such as The News Huddlines.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowding closely into a group, as a team does to talk tactics, is gathering.

parts.note: plays on the northern English saying where there's muck there's brass, brass being slang for money

explanation.surface: Northern wisdom that dirty work pays well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' is British slang for money, and 'where there's muck there's brass' says dirty jobs make money; the money is pictured as dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: Money gained dishonourably is described as dirty, matching the muck in the saying.

clue.text: Counterfeited next year's coins and prospered

definitions.meaning: faked money in advance, coins made before their time

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading treats the phrase literally: forged coins dated ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Faking coins in advance is a punning reading; making steady progress is the idiom's real meaning.

clue.text: Endless sorrow round at home for the alcoholic

indicators.note: the shortened sorrow goes around the word for at home
the final letter of the word for sorrow is cut off

parts.note: woe is sorrow
in means at home

explanation.surface: A drinker's grief that never stops, with drinks at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims the sorrow word to WO, and 'round' wraps those two letters about the home word; 'for the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A down-and-out heavy drinker is called by this slang term.

parts.note: firm is read as a business company, though the phrase means steadfast companions

explanation.surface: People whose relationship goes beyond work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' as a business is the misleading sense; the phrase means close and loyal.
explanation.definitionFit: Close loyal companions are more than people who simply know each other through work.

parts.note: tag is a children's chasing game

explanation.surface: A remark that some sport comes from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Game' means hunted animals; the second is a playground game.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer is hunted, so it counts as quarry.

indicators.note: variety suggests a mixed assortment, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A clergyman applauding a music-hall performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' looks like part of 'variety show' but signals rearranging CURATE CLAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A lavish staged entertainment is called by this noun.

clue.text: Less popular record brings back complaint

parts.note: slipped means fallen in popularity
a disc is a record

explanation.surface: An unpopular record bringing back an old grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brings back' seems to be one phrase, but 'back' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A displaced spinal cushion is a painful ailment of the spine.

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests pushed back, so the word for impudence is turned around

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk
grim means stern

explanation.surface: Cheek being sharply rejected by a severe person on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuffed' turns LIP into PIL; 'by' joins it to GRIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A person journeying to a holy place is a traveller.

parts.note: refers to the phrase make ..., meaning to enjoy oneself

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic remark about crafting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' suggests crafting something, but the answer completes the phrase 'make ___'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jolly and cheerful, and paired with 'make' it means to have a good time.

clue.text: Put off by act that included a song

indicators.note: included means the word for act holds the song within it

parts.note: a deed is an act
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: Being postponed because a performance had a song added.
explanation.definitionFit: Postponed or held back is a synonym of being put off.

indicators.note: out suggests being put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone declaring they would act on instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals rearranging the letters of I'D and ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Authoritative pronouncements are commands, the Latin plural of dictum.

clue.text: Back a favourite I'd found not so hot

indicators.note: back means the word for a favourite is read in reverse

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A punter backing a favourite and finding it disappointing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' sounds like betting, but turns PET into TEP; 'found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm, neither warm nor cold, is less than hot.
A reproduction is the first sense; text written for a newspaper is the second.
Luxuriant and opulent is one sense; slang for a heavy drinker is the other.

clue.text: Beastly way for Caesar to address his killer

definitions.text: way for Caesar to address his killer
definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's Caesar speaks to Brutus with the Latin vocative form

explanation.walkthrough: In Julius Caesar the dying Caesar says 'Et tu, ...?' to Brutus, using the Latin vocative.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage and animal-like is one sense; the vocative of Brutus, from 'Et tu', is the other.

definitions.meaning: a sudden rupture, as of a tyre
informal word for a big feast

explanation.definitionFit: A tyre bursting is one sense; a huge feast is the other.
To commit by contract is one sense; to hire a performer or reserve is the other.

indicators.note: reviewed suggests looked at again and revised, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A critic assessing a play by someone called Ted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' signals rearranging PLAY and TED.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something skilfully means performing it with expertise.

indicators.note: into suggests the letters being made into a new word, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A highway leading across a border into a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals rearranging the letters of ROAD RAN; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small principality in the Pyrenees is a European nation.

indicators.note: some means only part of the clue words gun-dogs is used

explanation.surface: Releasing a few hunting dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' signals letters taken from inside 'gun-dogs'.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten or untie something sets it free.

clue.text: Family loaf started off in oven

indicators.note: in places the opening letter of loaf inside the word for family

parts.note: kin means family

indicators.note: started off picks the opening letter of the word loaf

explanation.surface: A family loaf beginning to bake in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family loaf' reads as a bread size, but the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: A furnace for firing pottery or drying is a kind of oven.

clue.text: Leave and say nothing? My word!

parts.note: to go is to leave
sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: Someone told to depart and keep quiet, reacting with surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise.

parts.note: a comeback read literally as sound coming back off a surface

explanation.surface: A triumphant return to form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback' suggests a sporting revival; here it is sound returning.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflected sound returns to the listener.

parts.note: one over the eight usually means a drink too many, but the eight is a rowing crew and one person is in charge of it

explanation.surface: Someone who has had a drink too many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is British slang for being slightly drunk; an eight is also a rowing crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer supervises an eight-oared crew.

clue.text: An addition to Eastern part of a church

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is an addition to a letter

explanation.surface: An extension built at the east end of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A semicircular recess at the end of a church is a section of the building.

clue.text: How near David got to Goliath?

definitions.text: How near David got to Goliath?

parts.words: How near David got to Goliath?
parts.note: David felled Goliath with a sling, so the distance is the range of the missile he used

explanation.surface: A question about the closeness of the Biblical duel.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means a short distance, and David killed Goliath with a slingshot.
explanation.definitionFit: A short distance is the idiom's meaning, literally the range of a hurled rock.
